```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

`ontologyAPI` serves one ontology over two protocols, REST and the Model
Context Protocol (MCP), from a single set of handlers. You build an
`ontology_service()` once and hand it to either server, or both.

## 1. Build the service

```{r service}
library(ontologyAPI)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "aviation.duckdb")
svc <- ontology_service(
  ontologySpecR::spec_example_bundle(),   # or a bundle JSON path
  con,
  actor = "analyst"
)
svc
```

The service holds the normalised bundle and the `objectSetsR`, `conceptR` and
`actionTypesR` contexts. To run R action handlers, register them now:

```{r handlers}
svc$action_ctx <- actionTypesR::register_handler(
  svc$action_ctx, "UpdateAirportStatus",
  function(connection, action, params, target_ids) {
    # ... update the rows for target_ids ...
    list(updated = length(target_ids))
  }
)
```

Optionally restrict what callers may do, for both protocols:

```{r auth}
svc <- ontology_service(bundle, con, actor = "analyst",
  auth = function(actor, operation, resource) operation != "submit_action")
```

## 2. Serve REST

```{r rest}
serve_ontology(svc, port = 8080L)   # Swagger UI at /__docs__/
```

Set `ONTOLOGY_API_KEY`, or pass `api_key =`, to require
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`.

```{r httr2}
library(httr2)
base <- "http://127.0.0.1:8080"

request(paste0(base, "/v1/objects/Airport/query")) |>
  req_body_json(list(
    filters = list(list(property = "country", op = "eq", value = "Ireland")),
    limit = 50
  )) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

# Routes departing Dublin: the RouteOrigin link runs FlightRoute -> Airport,
# so from an Airport this is the reverse direction.
request(paste0(base, "/v1/objects/Airport/DUB/search_around/RouteOrigin")) |>
  req_method("POST") |>
  req_body_json(list(limit = 10)) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()
```

## 3. Serve MCP

```{r mcp}
serve_mcp(svc)                          # stdio, for Claude Desktop
serve_mcp(svc, transport = "sse", port = 3000L)
```

Add your own tools before serving:

```{r add-tool}
server <- mcp_server(svc, name = "aviation")
mcp_add_tool(server, "irish_airports", "List airports in Ireland",
  input_schema = list(type = "object", properties = list()),
  handler = function(params, server) {
    ontologyAPI:::h_query(server$svc, "Airport",
      filters = list(list(property = "country", op = "eq", value = "Ireland")))
  })
serve_mcp(server)
```

## 4. Filters

Both protocols take the same `filters` array of `{property, op, value}`
objects. The ops are `eq`, `neq`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`,
`starts_with`, `in`, `not_in`, `is_null` and `is_not_null`. Values are
injected into `objectSetsR::os_filter()` as R values, never pasted into SQL.

## 5. Actions

```{r action}
request(paste0(base, "/v1/actions/UpdateAirportStatus/submit")) |>
  req_body_json(list(
    params     = list(new_status = "maintenance"),
    target_ids = list("DUB"),
    dry_run    = TRUE
  )) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()
```

Over REST, `dry_run` defaults to `false`. The MCP `submit_action` tool
defaults to `true`, so agents preview the plan before changing anything.
